in_hebrew.name: ליאון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ליאון נגזר מהמילה העברית 'אריה', שפירושה 'לב האלוהים' או 'אריה האל'. הוא קשור קשר הדוק למילה היוונית 'Λέων', שגם היא מתייחסת לאריה. השם מופיע בתנ"ך כסמל לגבורה וכוח.

in_greek.name: Λέων
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Λέων προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη για το λιοντάρι, συμβολίζοντας το θάρρος και τη δύναμη. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα αυτό δεν αναφέρεται άμεσα, αλλά η λέξη 'Λέων' χρησιμοποιείται για να περιγράψει το λιοντάρι ως σύμβολο ισχύος.

in_latin.name: Leo
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Leo derivatur a Latina voce 'leo', quae regem bestiarum significat. In Ecclesia primitiva, Leo erat symbolum fortitudinis et potestatis. Nomen etiam associatur cum Papa Leone I, qui fuit unus de maximis Papis in historia Ecclesiae.

in_english.name: Léon
in_english.meaning: Léon means lion-like, brave as a lion
in_english.long_meaning: The name Léon originates from the Hebrew word 'lion', which symbolizes courage and strength. It was adopted into Greek as 'Λέων' (Léōn) and then into Latin as 'Leo'. In Christian tradition, Léon represents bravery and valor. The name is associated with several saints, including Saint Leo the Great, Pope from 440 to 461 AD.

data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian faith, the lion is a symbol of Christ, with St. Mark's gospel referring to Jesus as "the lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David." Hence, the name Léon can be understood to mean 'little lion of God' or 'God's lion cub,' reflecting the spiritual warrior nature of a Christian and the strength that comes from God. It also represents the idea of being a protector, as Christ is our shield and defender.

historical_references.reference: Leon I, also known as Leo the Great, was a pope of the Catholic Church from 440 to 461 AD. He is considered one of the greatest popes in history due to his efforts to defend Rome against the Visigoths and the Vandals, as well as his role in the Councils of Ephesus and Chalcedon.

Leon of Rhodes, also known as Leo the Wise, was a Byzantine Greek monk, theologian, and writer who lived in the 5th century AD. He is best known for his writings on theological and philosophical topics, particularly his commentary on the works of Dionysius the Areopagite.
